Subject: SLA template questions / monthly remedy structure

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking this on. As we work toward an SLA we can include in our contract, Acme has a few clarifying asks so procurement can proceed:

- Baseline availability: we currently expect 99.95% monthly uptime for core inference endpoints. Can Redwood confirm standard template language and whether 99.9% is supported for larger commitments?
- Remedy calculation: our procurement team prefers a simple, predictable monthly remedy (either X% of monthly invoice per band or an absolute cap). We need to understand the formula the vendor uses for credits and any caps.
- Latency commitments: we use P50/P95/P99 for tail latency commitments. Can you provide a recommended latency SLO set and how latency-induced remedies are handled, if at all?
- Maintenance carve-outs: we need clear language for planned maintenance windows, emergency maintenance, and coordinated upgrade carve-outs (notice windows, max monthly minutes).

I've attached our draft request and a one-month traffic sample to help size the economics.

Attachments: [Attachment: Acme-SLA-requests.pdf (pdf)], [Attachment: monthly_traffic_report.csv (csv)]

Appreciate a proposal by end of next week so we can route to legal.

Best,

Subject: Re: SLA template questions / monthly remedy structure

Hi Erin — thanks for the clear list and the attachments. Quick responses below, and I've sketched two practical options that map to common customer preferences.

Summary answers:
- Baseline availability: our standard hosted template offers 99.95% for enterprise agreements, 99.9% for self-serve/entry tiers. We can include either number in the SOW depending on commitment level.
- Remedy calculation: we support two remedy models:
  1) Percentage-based credits: monthly credit equal to (% below target) * monthly invoice capped at a configurable percentage (typically 50% of monthly invoice).
  2) Tiered bands: fixed credit buckets per band (e.g., 99.95–99.90 = 10% credit, 99.90–99.00 = 30%, <99.00 = 50%) with an absolute monthly cap (e.g., $250k).
- Latency: we recommend defining P95 and P99 windows for API-response time per model route; remedies for latency are rarer but can be added as a separate band tied to sustained P99 > threshold for longer than X minutes.
- Maintenance carve-outs: standard is 4 hours/month planned maintenance with 72-hour advance notice for non-critical work; emergency maintenance is carved out when no notice is possible, with post-facto notification and remediation reporting.

I'm attaching a short options sheet that lays out the two remedy models and sample calculations using your traffic file. Would you like a quick call tomorrow to walk through numbers?

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-sla-options-20260314.pdf (pdf)]

Thanks,

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@acmecommerce.com>, jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template questions / monthly remedy structure

Erin — looping in a quick commercial view from our side. Two practical points to make the remedy deterministic for procurement:

1) Formula proposal (percentage model):
- Observed uptime U = (seconds_up / seconds_in_month) * 100
- If U < SLO, monthly_credit = min( ((SLO - U) / SLO) * monthly_invoice, monthly_invoice * 0.5 )
- Example: SLO 99.95%, observed 99.80% -> (0.15 / 99.95) * invoice ≈ 0.15% of invoice (small). We typically apply banded multipliers so the credit is meaningful for large outages.

2) Banding (preferred for clarity):
- 99.95–99.90: 10% credit
- 99.90–99.00: 30% credit
- <99.00: 50% credit (absolute cap applies)

3) Absolute cap options: choose between a relative cap (50% of monthly invoice) or a fixed dollar cap (we can set a fixed cap once we see typical invoice size; suggests $200k default for first year).

4) Latency carve-in: we can offer an optional add-on that triggers a 10% credit band if P99 > 2s for more than 60 minutes sustained across the reporting window.

Operational notes: credits are applied to the next invoice; dispute window 30 days; reconciliation monthly.

Happy to sketch the SOW language if this matches what Acme wants.

—Ben

Director, Sales — Enterprise | Redwood Inference

Thanks Jasmine & Ben — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from legal and platform engineering after reviewing your proposals: 

- Legal would prefer the band percentages but wants a fixed dollar cap instead of a relative cap. Can Redwood provide a suggested fixed cap range once you see a monthly run rate? We're targeting a first-year cap of ~$150k but are open.
- Engineering asked for clearer latency SLO examples by route (e.g., /v1/generate P95 < 300ms, P99 < 900ms). They also want to understand degradation behavior: is there an automatic fallback to a lower-latency model variant and how does that interact with availability calculations?
- Maintenance notice: 72 hours for standard ops is fine but can we add a maximum monthly planned maintenance exposure (e.g., no more than 6 hours/month unless agreed)?

We added a few inline redlines to the attached request doc. If you can send a redlined SOW and a short ops playbook that shows incident notification, measurement method, and monthly reconciliation steps, legal and platform can move to signature.

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@acmecommerce.com>, jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template questions / monthly remedy structure — ops playbook draft

Hi Erin — thanks for the redlines. I put together a short ops playbook stub that we can include in the SOW appendix. High level: 

- Measurement method:
  - Uptime measured at the edge layer (HTTP 200 success and model inference completion) across the tenant's regional endpoints; calculation is seconds_up / seconds_in_month.
  - Latency measured from our public API gateway P95/P99 window; spikes are smoothed over 5-minute buckets for reporting.
- Incident notification:
  - T0 (detection): automated alert to Acme on-call (pager + email) within 5 minutes of threshold breach.
  - T1 (response): initial triage within 30 minutes; status updates every 30 minutes until resolved.
  - Post-incident: RCA within 72 hours for severity-high outages.
- Maintenance and carve-outs:
  - Planned maintenance: max 6 hours/month by default, 72-hour notice.
  - Emergency maintenance: carved out of SLA when immediate mitigation is required; we will provide post-event notification.
- Reconciliation and credits:
  - Monthly automated report (first business day of month) with uptime, latency, and any applicable credits. Dispute window 30 days. Credits applied to the next invoice.

Attachment: [Attachment: ops-playbook-stub.md (md)]

I also opened OPS-441 in our Jira with a proposed runbook; linking here for transparency: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/OPS-441. Happy to iterate the playbook with Acme engineering.

—Monica Patel
